The mutation incorrectly changes the boundary check from `x > hi` (which is logically sound for returning `hi` when `x` exceeds the upper limit) to `x >= hi`, causing the function to return `hi` prematurely when `x` equals `hi`. This breaks the requirement that the function should only clamp values strictly greater than `hi`. The fix is to revert the condition back to `x > hi`.
The bug is that the second condition incorrectly checks `x < hi` instead of `x > hi`, causing the function to return the upper bound when the input should remain unchanged. This logic error prevents the function from correctly clamping values that fall within the valid range `[lo, hi]`.

Fix: Change `x < hi` to `x > hi`.
